newsitem.title: UK: Copper advances again in LME evening, others follo.
newsitem.headline: Copper advances again in LME evening, others follo.

text.p: Copper prices continued to drive higher during Wednesday evening inter-office LME trading, and closed sharply higher.
Other metals were pulled upwards as well, with aluminium, zinc and nickel adding to the gains seen earlier during the open-outcry sessions.
"It is very much Comex-driven (on copper), but I think we might we approaching a sell-zone soon," one trader said.
Nevertheless, copper prices spurted another $30 during the evening, building on the near-$40 advance notched up by the end of the Wednesday kerb.
The trend in the spreads was supportive, with cash/threes months having whipped back above $200 backwardation to stand at $220 at 1900 gmt.
Three months prices were indicated at $2,270/75 a tonne, up from the $2,240 1700 kerb close, and Tuesday's $2,204.
The market in now in territory where selling is likely, with upside targets at $2,300 and ultimately $2,313, they added.
Aluminium pushed up to stand at $1,633/35 a tonne, near the $1,640/50 level where producer sales are expected.
Elsewhere, the influence of fund buying helped carry nickel to a 7-1/2 month high of $7,880/7,900 and zinc to a new two-year peak of $1,188/90.
